_about: The lands as one continent, each a shape of its own, painted by tools/world_layout.py from `design` (edit that and rerun it): each land's middle in world cells (x east, y north) lobes round it [dx, dy, across, up, turn°] and `area`, how many cells it comes out (about as big as its map was); a town's walled square (maps.json town.size) sits in its own countryside. The lands are one landmass with one coast. `lands`: the world cell each land's box (its map, maps.json width × height) starts on, south-west. `middles`: its middle in its own cells. `roads`: where each road crosses its border, the last cell on its side (`at`, its own cells; the next over, the way the exit goes, is the other land's), and the turns it takes there from the hub (`via`, out from the middle). `rivers`: each from its spring to the sea (or into a lake of its own, `lake` cells across), through the turns of its `course` (world cells), widening over its `width` [at the spring, at the sea]; `line`, its middle a cell apart, is the tool's. `regions`: its shape over its box and `margin` cells round it, row by row from the south, as runs of [code, length]: 1 its own land, 2 the sea it draws (the sea nearest it), 3 its own land under a river, 4 a land next door's under a river, 0 neither. check_content.py checks it fits maps.json.
